title: A virtual key call to a model
lede: The application calls the gateway route for its provider with a virtual key; the gateway swaps in the real key and the caller's key is never forwarded.

edges.label: virtual key on the provider route

steps.title: Call the provider route
steps.what: The application presents the virtual key as a bearer token or API-key header on the route for its provider.
steps.why: Applications and agents never hold the real provider key.

steps.title: The gateway checks the key
steps.what: In the requests tested: key valid (401), guardrail (400 naming the category), provider match (403 wrong provider), model on the list (403 not allowed).
steps.why: Model-route refusals name their cause in the response body, unlike bare MCP and A2A 403s.

steps.title: The real key is injected
steps.what: Privilege stores the provider key and injects it server-side; the caller's gateway key is never forwarded to the provider.
steps.why: The request-rate cap is enforced natively: bursts on a capped key were partly refused with 429 rate_limit_exceeded.
